### Context Map

**Issue / alert** — [GitHub Issue #490](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/490) — "Add a strict run path for pre-primed explore sessions". Status `OPEN`, no labels, assignee `@awinogradov (just assigned)`, no comments.

Summary of the body: [`/autopilot:explore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) primes a session and writes a durable `.claude/context/brief.md`, but [`/autopilot:run`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md) unconditionally re-runs the full [`gather-context`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md) fan-out in its Phase 1, so forking a primed session into a clean checkout of the same revision buys nothing. Proposal: a **separate** strict entry point (tentatively `/autopilot:run-primed`) that (1) requires the brief, (2) validates the brief's `Base:` SHA against the checkout's base, (3) uses the brief's stable sections in place of the broad codebase fan-out, (4) still resolves task-specific volatile context (issue/alert, branch/worktree/preflight, git state, narrow task-specific file reads), (5) continues through the existing `run` pipeline with no plan-approval gate, and (6) **fails loudly** — never silently downgrading to ordinary `run`. Explicitly: keep `/autopilot:run` unchanged, no heuristic branch inside `run`, and the skill must not know how the transcript or brief was persisted. Acceptance criteria name tests for valid / missing / stale / revision-mismatch cases and documentation of the orchestration flow, including that a transcript alone is insufficient without the validated brief. Related: #487 added the durable brief while leaving `plan`/`run` unchanged.

**Related TODOs** — No related TODOs found (0 matches for `#490`, `issues/490`, or a TODO/FIXME naming 490).

**Relevant files**

- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) — writes the brief; owns `Base:`, the fixed section order, and the stable/volatile split the new skill must validate and consume.
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md) — the flow to mirror: 8-task protocol, Phase 1 `gather-context`, Phase 2 preflight, Phase 3 shared pipeline, Phase 4/5 branch + automated commit→PR→monitor chain. Must stay byte-unchanged in behavior.
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md) — the fan-out being bypassed; its Context Map section list is the vocabulary the brief's sections map back to.
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/pipeline.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/pipeline.md) — the shared draft/review/finalize pipeline both `plan` and `run` execute; a third caller must reuse it, not copy it.
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/input-detection.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/input-detection.md) — detection table + tracker gating (create-issue flags are plan-only).
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/branch-blocks.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/branch-blocks.md) and [`stack-deltas.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/stack-deltas.md) — the `## Pre-Implementation` bodies (with `--autopilot` run variants) and the three per-stack values.
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/agents/resolve-issue-context.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/agents/resolve-issue-context.md) — the one resolver the primed path still needs; `digest-branch-diff`/`digest-repo-standards` are what the brief replaces.
- [`.github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts), [`linkResolution.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/linkResolution.test.ts), [`planFileOutputPurity.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/planFileOutputPurity.test.ts) — the three discovery-driven guards a new skill directory is automatically enrolled in.
- [`.github/actions/code-review-action/src/markdownFiles.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/markdownFiles.ts) — `walkMarkdown`, the shared tree walk any new guard test reuses.
- [`scripts/validate-plugins.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/scripts/validate-plugins.ts) + [`scripts/schemas.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/scripts/schemas.ts) — `bun run validate` discovers `claude-plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md` by glob and checks frontmatter against `skillFrontmatterSchema`.
- [`claude-plugins/autopilot/README.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/README.md) — Structure tree, Slash Skills section, Internal Skills section: all need the new entry.
- [`README.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/README.md) — the numbered Repository-docs table; a new chapter needs a row.
- [`docs/14-explore-skill.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/docs/14-explore-skill.md) — the brief's contract as documented, incl. the explicit line "`plan`, `run`, and `commits-create` do not consume it", which this change makes stale.
- [`docs/05-plan-run-skills.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/docs/05-plan-run-skills.md) — how the plan/run flow is documented (ASCII diagrams, phase-by-phase, sub-agent JSON contracts).
- [`.gitignore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.gitignore) / [`.prettierignore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.prettierignore) — `.claude/context/` is ignored by both; the brief is never committed, which is exactly why the new skill must validate rather than assume.

**Patterns to mirror**

- **Reference-over-copy** — `run` does not restate `plan`'s input resolution or Common Instructions; it links to them (`../plan/SKILL.md#input-resolution`). A third caller must do the same for the pipeline, branch blocks, and stack deltas. `explore/SKILL.md` states the rule outright: "Do not re-implement the fan-out here. It has one owner."
- **Explicit separate contract over heuristic branch** — the issue demands it, and it matches how `plan` vs `run` split (both mode calls live in the orchestrator "outside the shared pipeline, so `run` cannot reach them").
- **Fail loudly on a stale artifact** — `gather-context`'s failure handling: a *resolver* failure is fatal ("surface the error and stop, so nothing proceeds against a misfetched target"); a *digest* failure is degraded-not-wrong. A stale brief is the former.
- **Base-SHA classification** — `explore` Phase 0 already owns the exact staleness test (`git fetch origin main`, then a `<base>..origin/main` diff with the four derived-path exclusions, plus "a `<base>` that no longer resolves ⇒ full prime"). The new skill's validation is the same predicate with a *reject* verdict instead of a *re-prime* verdict; that logic has one owner and should be cited, not re-derived.
- **Task Progress Protocol** — numbered TaskCreate table, each task `in_progress` at phase start and `completed` at phase end.
- **Frontmatter shape** — `name`, `description`, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools` (an explicit allowlist including `Skill(autopilot:*)` entries; note skills are referenced with the hyphen form `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)` while directories use the colon form).
- **Discovery-not-hardcoded tests** — every skill guard walks `readdir`/`walkMarkdown` and asserts a floor (`expect(skillDirs.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)`), with opt-outs named in a `Set` plus a reason comment.
- **Reference formatting** — every skill ends with a directive pointing at [`shared-rules/references/reference-formatting.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/shared-rules/references/reference-formatting.md) plus the MANDATORY self-check paragraph; `sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts` fails any new skill that lacks it, and also fails one that *re-inlines* the block text.

**Key types**

- `skillFrontmatterSchema` (Zod, [`scripts/schemas.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/scripts/schemas.ts)) — `{ name (kebab, `:` allowed), description, argument-hint?, allowed-tools?, model? }`; non-strict, so `user-invocable: false` passes through.
- `walkMarkdown(dir): Promise<string[]>` — the shared markdown tree walk.
- `InsertBody { file, line, heading, content }` — plan-file insert bodies discovered by fence + heading.
- `Reference { label, sourceFile, filePath, anchor }` — link-resolution records.
- The **brief** itself is prose, not a schema: `Base: <sha>` plus nine fixed `##` sections (six stable, three volatile). There is no parser today — the validation contract this issue asks for is new.

**Test conventions**

- `bun test`, run through `turbo run test`; tests are `*.test.ts` beside their subject under `src/`, using `describe`/`test`/`expect` from `bun:test` and `test.each` for per-item cases.
- Skill-markdown guards live in [`.github/actions/code-review-action/src/`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/tree/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src) (`sharedRulesInvocation`, `planFileOutputPurity`, `linkResolution`, `sharedBlockSync`, `rulesDocUrlSync`), resolving `repoRoot` via `join(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "..")`.
- Each guard opens with a JSDoc block stating what it guards **and what it cannot prove** (e.g. "CI sees text in a file, nothing more … Runtime evidence comes from the dry-run recorded on the PR"). Match that.
- Failures assert on a labelled string (`expect(\`${label} has "${token}": ${…}\`).toBe(…)`) so the message names the item, the token, and the reason.
- Repo-wide gates: `bun run lint` = `format:check` + `validate` + `typecheck`. Per memory, `bun run lint`/`turbo run test` are already red on `main` (prettier-drifted CHANGELOGs, a zod `.loose()` issue) — verify only authored files.
- The worktree needs `bun install` before tests/typecheck will run.

**In-flight changes** — Branch `sotol-shale` carries one commit, `revert(code-review): restore pull_request trigger for ai-review` (touching `.github/workflows/code-review.yml` and `.github/actions/code-review-action/action.yml`). `isStaleMerged: true` — that work already landed upstream under a rewritten SHA. `baseAhead: 26`: the checkout predates both explore commits, so `skills/explore/`, `skills/gather-context/`, `skills/shared-rules/`, `docs/13`, and `docs/14` are **absent from the working tree** and were read from `origin/main`.

**Applicable standards**

- **[RFC-0001](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/rfc/0001-reference-formatting.md) — Reference formatting & readability, status Accepted (currently v6).** Every reference in the new SKILL.md, the docs chapter, and the READMEs must be a resolvable link; `linkResolution.test.ts` enforces it mechanically over `skills/`, `agents/`, `docs/`, `rfc/`, `README.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. As of v6 skills **read** the block from `shared-rules` rather than inlining it — re-inlining fails `sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts`.
- Dropped candidates: none — `rfc/` holds exactly one RFC, and there is no `principles/` directory.
- Repo conventions in force (from [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) / [`docs/01-workspace-structure.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/docs/01-workspace-structure.md) / [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)): no over-engineering, no unrequested abstraction; camelCase names incl. constants; named exports only; interfaces over types; JSDoc on exported types; branch `issue-490-<slug>`; conventional commits, lowercase imperative subject ≤50 chars, body required for `feat:`; PR title capitalized, business-focused, no issue number.

**Stack** — `agents.rules: "Bun"`, `agents.language: "typescript"` → the Bun stack deltas in [`stack-deltas.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/stack-deltas.md). Set task 2 complete. Now the intent gate.

### Steelmanned Intent

A separate, explicit `/autopilot:run-primed` entry point that consumes a SHA-validated explore brief instead of the broad context fan-out, and fails loudly rather than silently downgrading to `run`.

### Assumptions

- New skill directory `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run-primed/` (hyphen form, user-invocable) — a separate contract, never a flag or heuristic branch inside `run`.
- `run/SKILL.md` stays behaviorally unchanged; at most it gains a "see also" pointer.
- "The exact repository base used by the current clean checkout" means the brief's `Base:` SHA compared against the checkout's `origin/main`, reusing the same derived-path exclusions [`explore` Phase 0](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md#phase-0-classify-the-run) already defines — but with a *reject* verdict where `explore` re-primes.
- Docs land as a new numbered chapter 15 plus a row in the [README](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/README.md#repository-docs) table, rather than expanding chapter 14.
- The repomix `outputId` recorded in the brief is session-scoped, so the primed path re-attaches `.repomix/pack.xml` rather than reusing the recorded id.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/tony_vi/.claude/plugins/cache/code-assistants/autopilot/1.14.0/skills/ascii-schemas

# ASCII Schemas

Generate ASCII schemas, diagrams, and UI wireframes using Unicode box-drawing characters following wiretext conventions. Output renders correctly in any monospace environment — terminals, markdown, code blocks, GitHub PRs, and plain text documents.

## When to Use

**Technical schemas:**

- Architecture diagrams in implementation plans
- Entity-relationship models for database design
- Deployment and infrastructure topologies
- Data flow and component interaction diagrams
- Sequence and timeline diagrams

**UI wireframes:**

- Screen mockups for feature planning
- Page layout prototypes
- Mobile app screen flows
- Dashboard and admin panel wireframes
- Component library documentation

## MCP Integration

If the `@wiretext/mcp` server is connected, prefer its tools for UI wireframes — they handle component positioning and rendering automatically:

- **`create_wireframe`** — returns an editable wiretext.app URL from wire objects
- **`render_wireframe`** — returns ASCII art from wire objects

Wire object format:

```json
{
  "type": "component",
  "componentType": "navbar",
  "position": { "col": 0, "row": 0 },
  "width": 50,
  "navItems": ["Home", "Products", "About"]
}
```

Available component types: `button`, `input`, `select`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `toggle`, `table`, `modal`, `browser`, `card`, `navbar`, `tabs`, `progress`, `avatar`, `divider`, `breadcrumb`, `list`, `stepper`, `rating`, `skeleton`, `alert`, `image`, `icon`.

Primitives: `box`, `text`, `line`, `arrow`.

Fall back to hand-drawn ASCII when the MCP server is not connected or for technical schemas (architecture, ER, topology, sequence diagrams).

## Core Rules

1. **Width guideline: 80 characters** for technical schemas. Wireframes may extend wider when layout requires it, but aim for minimal width
2. **Default border style: single** — use `┌─┐│└┘` as the default. Use rounded `╭─╮│╰╯` for mobile frames, chat bubbles, and softer cards. Use double `╔═╗║╚╝` for emphasis (invoices, highlighted pricing). Use heavy `┏━┓┃┗┛` for critical elements (deploy targets, warnings)
3. **Annotation-free diagrams** — never overlay prose on diagram borders or arrows. Put explanations in a separate "Flow Legend" section below the diagram
4. **Strip trailing whitespace** — no trailing spaces on any line
5. **Monospace assumed** — every character occupies exactly one grid cell
6. **Wrap in code block** — always present diagrams inside triple-backtick fenced code blocks

## Character Quick Reference

### Box Drawing

| Style   | Corners         | Horizontal | Vertical | Tees                |
| ------- | --------------- | ---------- | -------- | ------------------- |
| Single  | `┌` `┐` `└` `┘` | `─`        | `│`      | `├` `┤` `┬` `┴` `┼` |
| Double  | `╔` `╗` `╚` `╝` | `═`        | `║`      | `╠` `╣`             |
| Rounded | `╭` `╮` `╰` `╯` | `─`        | `│`      | `├` `┤`             |
| Heavy   | `┏` `┓` `┗` `┛` | `━`        | `┃`      | `┣` `┫`             |

### Arrows and Connectors

| Character       | Usage                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------ |
| `→` `←` `↑` `↓` | Directional flow         |
| `▶` `◀` `▼` `▲` | Emphasized flow          |
| `↗` `↘`         | Trend indicators         |
| `──▶`           | Horizontal arrow line    |
| `◀──▶`          | Bidirectional connection |
| `──→`           | Screen-to-screen flow    |

### Flow References

Circled numerals for labeling flows — explain each in a legend below:

`①` `②` `③` `④` `⑤` `⑥` `⑦` `⑧` `⑨` `⑩`

### UI Symbols

| Character   | Usage                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `░`         | Image/content placeholder fill            |
| `▓`         | Progress bar filled portion               |
| `⌕`         | Search icon                               |
| `≡`         | Hamburger menu                            |
| `⍥`         | User/avatar icon                          |
| `▾`         | Dropdown arrow                            |
| `×`         | Close button                              |
| `⊕`         | Add/plus button                           |
| `✓`         | Checkmark / success                       |
| `●` `○`     | Filled/empty dot (status, ratings, radio) |
| `★`         | Star / logo placeholder                   |
| `♡` `¶`     | Like, comment icons                       |
| `◀` `▶` `■` | Media controls (prev, play, stop)         |

### UI Component Patterns

**Toggle switch:**

```
[●──] On label           [──●] Off label
```

**Checkbox:**

```
[✓] Checked item          [ ] Unchecked item
```

**Radio button:**

```
(●) Selected option       ( ) Unselected option
```

**Select/dropdown:**

```
┌──────────────────────┐
│ Selected value     ▾ │
└──────────────────────┘
```

**Progress bar:**

```
▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░
```

**Rating:**

```
●●●●○ (128 reviews)
```

**Stepper:**

```
● Account ─ ● Profile ─ ○ Plan ─ ○ Confirm
```

**Breadcrumb:**

```
Home / Shoes / Running / Air Max Pro
```

**Divider with label:**

```
── Section Title ──────────────────────
```

**Image placeholder:**

```
┌────────────────────────────────────┐
│░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
│░░░░░░░░░░░░Product Photo░░░░░░░░░░░│
│░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
└────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Technical Diagram Types

### 1. Architecture / Flow Diagram

Boxes represent components, arrows show data or control flow, circled numerals reference a flow legend.

```
┌──────────┐                              ┌──────────────┐
│  Browser  │───── ① ────────────────────▶│   Auth API   │
└──────────┘                              └──────┬───────┘
      │                                          │ ②
      │ ⑤                                       ▼
      │                                   ┌──────────────┐
      │                                   │   Session DB  │
      │                                   └──────────────┘
      │          ┌──────────────┐
      └── ③ ───▶│    IdP       │

                        │ ④
                        ▼
                 ┌──────────────┐

                 │  Callback    │
                 └──────────────┘
```

**Flow Legend:**

- ① Direct login: browser sends credentials to Auth API
- ② Auth API creates session in Session DB
- ③ SSO redirect: browser redirected to external IdP
- ④ IdP posts assertion back to SAML/OIDC callback
- ⑤ Browser receives session cookie after successful auth

### 2. Entity-Relationship Diagram

Table boxes with column annotations (`PK`, `FK`, `UQ`) and cardinality (`1`, `*`).

```
┌──────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────┐
│      user        │      │   organization   │
├──────────────────┤      ├──────────────────┤
```

```
   ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐
```

Use rounded boxes for stages, heavy for critical targets, connecting lines for flow:

```
╭────────────╮    ╭────────────╮    ╭────────────╮    ┏━━━━━━━━━━┓
│  Git Push  │────│   Build    │────│    Test    │────┃  Deploy  ┃
```

## UI Wireframe Patterns

### Browser Frame

Wrap any web page wireframe in a browser chrome:

### Pricing / Emphasis with Double Border

Use double border `╔═╗║╚╝` to highlight a featured element:

```
                         ╔════════════════════════╗
┌────────────────────────┐ ║ Pro — Most Popular     ║ ┌────────────────────────┐
│ Starter                │ ╠────────────────────────╣ │ Enterprise             │
├────────────────────────┤ ║ $29/mo                 ║ ├────────────────────────┤
│ of/mo                  │ ║ Unlimited Projects     ║ │ Custom                 │
│ 3 Projects             │ ║ Priority Support       ║ │ Unlimited Everything   │
│                        │ ║                        ║ │                        │
│ ┌────────────────────┐ │ ║ ┌────────────────────┐ ║ │ ┌────────────────────┐ │
│ │    Get Started     │ │ ║ │  Start Free Trial  │ ║ │ │   Contact Sales    │ │
│ └────────────────────┘ │ ║ └────────────────────┘ ║ │ └────────────────────┘ │
└────────────────────────┘ ╚════════════════════════╝ └────────────────────────┘
```

### Chat Bubbles

Use rounded corners. Left-align incoming, right-align outgoing:

```
╭────────────────────────────╮
│  Hey, are you free today?  │ 10:30 AM
╰────────────────────────────╯

          ╭────────────────────────────╮
10:32 AM  │    Sure! Coffee at 2pm?    │
          ╰────────────────────────────╯
```

## Construction Guidelines

### Box Sizing

- **Minimum height**: 3 rows (top border, content, bottom border)
- **Minimum width**: label length + 4 (2 padding each side)
- **Label centering**: center text horizontally within the box
- **Multi-row boxes**: use `├──────┤` tees as internal row separator
- **Text truncation**: use `…` when text exceeds available width

### Spacing and Alignment

- **Horizontal gap between boxes**: 1-2 characters minimum
- **Vertical gap between rows**: 1+ rows for arrow labels
- **Arrow lines**: `─` horizontal, `│` vertical
- **Arrow labels**: adjacent to the arrow line, never overlapping a box border
- **Alignment**: align box tops at the same logical level

### Flow Legend Format

Place after the diagram as a separate markdown section:

```
**Flow Legend:**
- ① Description of first flow
- ② Description of second flow
```

### Internal Subdivisions

For boxes with headers (tables, cards with title bars):

```
┌───────────────────┐
│   Section Title   │
├───────────────────┤
│ content row 1     │
│ content row 2     │
└───────────────────┘
```

### Border Style Selection

| Style   | When to Use                                               |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Single  | Default for technical schemas and most UI elements        |
| Rounded | Mobile frames, chat bubbles, cards, modals, soft UI       |
| Double  | Highlighted/featured elements (pricing, invoices, alerts) |
| Heavy   | Critical deployment targets, warnings, emphasis           |

**Mixing rule**: one alternative style per diagram to highlight a single element. Exception: wireframes may use rounded for the outer frame with single for inner components.

## Anti-Patterns

**Do not:**

- Place text annotations overlapping box borders
- Mix more than two border styles in one diagram
- Use diagrams for simple tabular data — prefer markdown tables
- Add purely decorative elements — keep diagrams functional
- Use full-width Unicode characters — they break grid alignment
- Forget code block wrapping — naked diagrams lose alignment
- Use inconsistent spacing between same-level elements

## Reference formatting

Before writing any output that mentions a file, standard, section, commit, or issue, read [`reference-formatting.md`](../shared-rules/references/reference-formatting.md) (RFC-0001) and apply it verbatim — link files, docs, skills, agents, and sections, and never leave a reference as bare text.

**Reference self-check (MANDATORY):** after composing the output, re-read it against [`reference-formatting.md`](../shared-rules/references/reference-formatting.md). A bare commit SHA, a bare tracker id outside a magic-word line, or an unlinked mention of a file that exists in the repo is a violation — fix it before emitting.

Both recommendations accepted. Preflight: the Context Map shows a stale-merged worktree branch 26 behind base, so the plan's Pre-Implementation block re-syncs and branches fresh — no interactive preflight needed.

# Add a strict run path for pre-primed explore sessions

## Pre-Implementation

Work happens on a new `issue-490-<slug>` branch created from an up-to-date `main`, so the pull request can close issue #490 on merge. The current worktree sits on a stale-merged branch 26 commits behind the base, so `main` is re-synced before the branch is cut — otherwise the work would carry finished history and would not even see the `explore` and `gather-context` skills it depends on.

## Summary

Add `/autopilot:run-primed`, a separate strict entry point that consumes a SHA-validated `.claude/context/brief.md` in place of the broad codebase fan-out, and extend `gather-context` with a third `Scope` value so the primed path still resolves everything the brief cannot bake in advance. `/autopilot:run` is untouched.

Steelmanned intent: A separate, explicit `/autopilot:run-primed` entry point that consumes a SHA-validated explore brief instead of the broad context fan-out, and fails loudly rather than silently downgrading to `run`.

Score: [pending review]

## Context

[Issue #490](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/490) describes an orchestration pattern that today buys nothing: run [`/autopilot:explore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) once on an immutable revision, persist the transcript and the durable brief, fork the session into a clean checkout of that same revision, then implement a tracked issue. Step four must call [`/autopilot:run`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md), whose Phase 1 unconditionally re-runs the entire [`gather-context`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md) fan-out. The forked transcript is visible to the model but is not an authoritative input, so the repository is mapped twice.

That contract is correct for interactive `run` and must stay. The fix is a second, explicit door — not a heuristic inside `run` that tries to decide whether conversation history can be trusted. A file on disk carrying a base SHA is checkable; a prompt claiming "context was already gathered" is not.

Two decisions were taken with the requester before drafting. The acceptance criterion asking for tests over valid / missing / stale / revision-mismatch briefs is satisfied by a **discovery-driven guard test over the skill markdown**, the way every other skill in this repository is tested ([`planFileOutputPurity.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/planFileOutputPurity.test.ts), [`sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts)) — no bundled validator runtime and no new workspace scaffolding. And the task-specific context the primed path still needs is obtained by extending `gather-context` with `Scope: primed`, exactly the additive, default-preserving way `broad` was added, rather than hand-copying its resolver roster into a second skill.

## Design

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     /autopilot:run-primed                      │
└───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ ①
                                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Phase 1 — Validate .claude/context/brief.md                   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  present?  ·  parses?  ·  Base: resolves?  ·  Base: == HEAD?   │
└───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┘
                │ ②                              │ ③
                ▼                                ▼
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓   ┌───────────────────────────────┐
┃  Abort                     ┃   │  Phase 2                      │
┃  missing · malformed       ┃   │  gather-context Scope: primed │
┃  stale · revision-mismatch ┃   └───────────────┬───────────────┘
┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛                   │ ④
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 3 — Preflight verdict  │
                                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 4 — Draft · review     │
                                 │  · score · finalize           │
                                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                 │ ⑤
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 5 — Branch · implement │
                                 │  · commit · PR · monitor      │
                                 └───────────────────────────────┘
```

**Flow Legend:**

- ① Same argument forms as `run`: GitHub issue, Linear id, code-scanning alert, or a description. Input detection is unchanged and performs no I/O.
- ② Any of the four failure modes stops the run with an actionable message naming `/autopilot:run` as the caller's explicit fallback. There is no automatic downgrade.
- ③ The brief validated; its six stable sections become the repository context.
- ④ Only what the brief cannot bake in advance: issue or alert resolution, TODO search, branch diff, git state, snapshot re-attach.
- ⑤ Phases 3 through 5 are the existing `run` phases, referenced rather than restated.

Which context comes from where:

```
┌──────────────────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  .claude/context/brief.md    │      │  gather-context              │
│  (stable, SHA-validated)     │      │  Scope: primed               │
├──────────────────────────────┤      ├──────────────────────────────┤
│  Architecture map            │      │  Issue / alert               │
│  Data flow                   │      │  Related TODOs               │
│  Conventions and standards   │      │  In-flight changes           │
│  Key types                   │      │  Git state                   │
│  Test and verify             │      │  Snapshot (re-attached)      │
└──────────────┬───────────────┘      └───────────────┬──────────────┘
               │ ⑥                                    │ ⑦
               └──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                   ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                   │  Working context for the     │
                   │  draft · review · implement  │
                   └──────────────────────────────┘
```

**Flow Legend:**

- ⑥ The brief's stable half only. Its own volatile sections are ignored — they were computed in the explore session, in a different checkout.
- ⑦ The repomix `outputId` recorded in the brief is session-scoped and dead in a forked session, so the pack is re-attached rather than reused.

### The validation contract

Four rejections and one acceptance, all resolvable from `git` with no network round trip:

| Verdict               | Test                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **missing**           | `<root>/.claude/context/brief.md` does not exist                         |
| **malformed**         | no `Base:` line, or any of the nine fixed `##` sections absent           |
| **revision-mismatch** | `Base:` does not resolve, or is not an ancestor of `HEAD`                |
| **stale**             | `Base:` is a strict ancestor of `HEAD` — an older revision of this line  |
| **valid**             | `Base:` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`                                      |

Comparing against `HEAD` rather than a freshly fetched `origin/main` is deliberate: the primed contract is an *exact-revision* contract, a clean checkout of the mapped revision has `HEAD` at that revision, and a fetch-based comparison would let a concurrent upstream merge fail a run that is in fact correctly primed. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` is what separates "older revision of this history" from "different history entirely", which is why the acceptance criteria's `stale` and `revision-mismatch` cases stay distinguishable.

## Implementation Steps

1. [ ] Create `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run-primed/SKILL.md`. Frontmatter mirrors `run/SKILL.md` (`name: run-primed`, description, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools`) with `Read` and `Bash(git *)` present for brief validation. Body carries: Phase 0 input detection pointing at [`input-detection.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/input-detection.md) (create-issue flags skipped, as in `run`); Phase 1 the validation contract above, each verdict with its literal abort message; Phase 2 the `gather-context` invocation with `Scope: primed`; Phase 3 the merge rule stating the brief supplies the stable half and the map the volatile half. Phases 4 and 5 are **links** into `run/SKILL.md`'s existing phases and the shared [`pipeline.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/pipeline.md) / [`branch-blocks.md`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/plan/references/branch-blocks.md), never a copy — `run` already sets that precedent by referencing `plan` for input resolution and Common Instructions. Close with the reference-formatting directive and the mandatory self-check, copied structurally from `run/SKILL.md` (a pointer, never the block text).
   - verify: `bun run validate` prints `✔ claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run-primed/SKILL.md`, and `bun test .github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts` passes — that test discovers skills by `readdir`, so it fails if the new skill lacks the directive or re-inlines a shared block.

2. [ ] Add `primed` to the `Scope` input in `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md`. In the Input section, document the third value. In Phase 1, gate `digest-repo-standards` off at `primed` — the brief's `## Conventions and standards` came from that same digest on the same revision, so re-running it is pure duplicate cost. `digest-branch-diff` **still runs**, because `isStaleMerged` and `baseAhead` describe this checkout, not the explore session's. In Phase 2, `primed` reads the snapshot only for task-specific gaps the brief does not cover. Phase 3's section list is unchanged; `Applicable standards` is written as supplied by the caller's brief.
   - verify: `bun test .github/actions/code-review-action/src/linkResolution.test.ts` passes, and the Scope table in the file lists exactly `task`, `broad`, `primed`.

3. [ ] Add `.github/actions/code-review-action/src/primedBriefContract.test.ts`, reusing `walkMarkdown` from [`markdownFiles.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/markdownFiles.ts). It asserts: the skill enumerates all four abort verdicts and the valid case; it carries no dispatch of the `run` skill, so it cannot silently downgrade; `run/SKILL.md` still invokes `gather-context` unconditionally and mentions no brief, guarding "ordinary run unchanged"; `gather-context/SKILL.md` documents all three `Scope` values. The load-bearing assertion is cross-file: extract the `##` section names from the brief template fence in `explore/SKILL.md` and assert `run-primed/SKILL.md` names the same stable set — that catches the real rot, a renamed brief section silently breaking the consumer. Open with the repository's standard JSDoc block stating what the test guards **and what it cannot prove** (CI sees text in a file, not a run; runtime evidence is a dry-run recorded on the PR).
   - verify: `bun test .github/actions/code-review-action/src/primedBriefContract.test.ts` passes; then temporarily rename one `##` heading in the brief template inside `explore/SKILL.md` and confirm the cross-file assertion fails, proving the guard bites rather than passing vacuously.

4. [ ] Documentation. Add `docs/15-run-primed-skill.md` as the next numbered chapter: why a separate contract beats a heuristic, the orchestration flow the caller owns, the validation table, and an explicit statement that a forked transcript alone is insufficient without the validated brief artifact. Add its row to the Repository-docs table in `README.md`. In `claude-plugins/autopilot/README.md`, add `run-primed/` to the Structure tree, a `### /autopilot:run-primed` entry beside `/autopilot:run`, and the third `Scope` value in the `gather-context` Internal Skills paragraph. In `docs/14-explore-skill.md`, correct the Brief-lifecycle bullet that currently states `plan`, `run`, and `commits-create` do not consume the brief — that becomes false — and cross-link chapter 15. No RFC content changes, so no `version` bump or Changelog entry is due.
   - verify: `bunx prettier@3.8.3 --check` passes on every edited `.md` (adding a row re-pads the whole README docs table), and `bun test .github/actions/code-review-action/src/linkResolution.test.ts` passes so every new link and anchor resolves.

## Files

- `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run-primed/SKILL.md` - the new strict entry point: validate, gather narrowly, delegate the tail (new)
- `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md` - third `Scope` value; `digest-repo-standards` gated off at `primed`
- `.github/actions/code-review-action/src/primedBriefContract.test.ts` - guard over the contract and the explore↔run-primed section coupling (new)
- `docs/15-run-primed-skill.md` - chapter 15: the orchestration flow and the artifact contract (new)
- `README.md` - Repository-docs table row 15
- `claude-plugins/autopilot/README.md` - Structure tree, Slash Skills entry, `gather-context` Scope paragraph
- `docs/14-explore-skill.md` - correct the "who does not read the brief" bullet; cross-link chapter 15

Untouched on purpose: `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md` (the acceptance criterion is that ordinary `run` is unchanged), `claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md` (it already writes everything needed), and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (version bumps are release-action's, driven by conventional commits).

## Verification

Run in a fresh checkout after `bun install` (a new worktree shares no `node_modules`):

- `bun run validate` — frontmatter of the new skill against the plugin schema
- `bun test .github/actions/code-review-action/src/` — the new guard plus `sharedRulesInvocation`, `linkResolution`, and `planFileOutputPurity`, all of which enroll the new skill by discovery
- `bunx prettier@3.8.3 --check` on the edited markdown only — never a whole-repo write; `bun run lint` and `turbo run test` are already red on `main` for unrelated reasons, so verify authored files rather than the repo total

End-to-end evidence CI cannot produce: record a dry run on the pull request showing `/autopilot:run-primed` rejecting a deliberately mismatched brief and accepting a matching one.

## Post-Implementation

Once every step above is done and verified:

1. Update any `README.md`, `docs/*`, and `rfc/*` this change affects, so the documented source of truth stays current. Editing the content of an Accepted RFC also means bumping its `version` frontmatter and adding a Changelog entry.
2. Then decide what to do with the work: commit it, open a pull request, or stop here.

input.content:
# Add a strict run path for pre-primed explore sessions

## Pre-Implementation

Work happens on a new `issue-490-<slug>` branch created from an up-to-date `main`, so the pull request can close issue #490 on merge. The current worktree sits on a stale-merged branch 26 commits behind the base, so `main` is re-synced before the branch is cut — otherwise the work would carry finished history and would not even see the `explore` and `gather-context` skills it depends on.

## Summary

Add `/autopilot:run-primed`, a separate strict entry point that consumes a SHA-validated `.claude/context/brief.md` in place of the broad codebase pass, and extend `gather-context` with a third `Scope` value so the primed path still resolves everything the brief cannot bake in advance. `/autopilot:run` is untouched.

Steelmanned intent: A separate, explicit `/autopilot:run-primed` entry point that consumes a SHA-validated explore brief instead of the broad context fan-out, and fails loudly rather than silently downgrading to `run`.

Score: 90/100 — weakest dimension **Testability**, explained under [Verification](#verification).

## Context

[Issue #490](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/490) describes an orchestration pattern that today buys nothing: run [`/autopilot:explore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) once on an immutable revision, persist the transcript and the durable brief, fork the session into a clean checkout of that same revision, then implement a tracked issue. Step four must call [`/autopilot:run`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md), whose Phase 1 unconditionally re-runs the entire [`gather-context`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md) fan-out. The forked transcript is visible to the model but is not an authoritative input, so the repository is mapped twice.

That contract is correct for interactive `run` and must stay. The fix is a second, explicit door — not a heuristic inside `run` that tries to decide whether conversation history can be trusted. A file on disk carrying a base SHA is checkable; a prompt claiming "context was already gathered" is not.

Two decisions were taken with the requester before drafting. The acceptance criterion asking for tests over valid / missing / stale / revision-mismatch briefs is satisfied by a **discovery-driven guard test over the skill markdown**, the way every other skill in this repository is tested ([`planFileOutputPurity.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/planFileOutputPurity.test.ts), [`sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts)) — no bundled validator runtime and no new workspace scaffolding. And the task-specific context the primed path still needs comes from extending `gather-context` with `Scope: primed`, the same additive, default-preserving way `broad` was added, rather than hand-copying its resolver roster into a second skill.

## Design

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     /autopilot:run-primed                      │
└───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ ①
                                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Phase 1 — Validate .claude/context/brief.md                   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  present?  ·  parses?  ·  Base: resolves?  ·  Base: is base?   │
└───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┘
                │ ②                              │ ③
                ▼                                ▼
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓   ┌───────────────────────────────┐
┃  Abort                     ┃   │  Phase 2                      │
┃  missing · malformed       ┃   │  gather-context Scope: primed │
┃  stale · revision-mismatch ┃   └───────────────┬───────────────┘
┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛                   │ ④
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 3 — Preflight verdict  │
                                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 4 — Draft · review     │
                                 │  · score · finalize           │
                                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                 │ ⑤
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 5 — Branch · implement │
                                 │  · commit · PR · monitor      │
                                 └───────────────────────────────┘
```

**Flow Legend:**

- ① Same argument forms as `run`: GitHub issue, Linear id, code-scanning alert, or a description. Input detection is unchanged and performs no I/O.
- ② Any of the four failure modes stops the run with an actionable message naming `/autopilot:run` as the caller's explicit fallback. There is no automatic downgrade.
- ③ The brief validated; five of its six stable sections become the repository context.
- ④ Only what the brief cannot bake in advance: issue or alert resolution, TODO search, branch diff, git state, snapshot re-attach.
- ⑤ Phases 3 through 5 are the existing `run` phases, referenced rather than restated.

Which context comes from where:

```
┌──────────────────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  .claude/context/brief.md    │      │  gather-context              │
│  (stable, SHA-validated)     │      │  Scope: primed               │
├──────────────────────────────┤      ├──────────────────────────────┤
│  Architecture map            │      │  Issue / alert               │
│  Data flow                   │      │  Related TODOs               │
│  Conventions and standards   │      │  In-flight changes           │
│  Key types                   │      │  Git state                   │
│  Test and verify             │      │  Snapshot (re-attached)      │
└──────────────┬───────────────┘      └───────────────┬──────────────┘
               │ ⑥                                    │ ⑦
               └──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                   ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                   │  Working context for the     │
                   │  draft · review · implement  │
                   └──────────────────────────────┘
```

**Flow Legend:**

- ⑥ Five of the brief's six stable sections. Its three volatile sections are ignored — they were computed in the explore session, in a different checkout.
- ⑦ `## Snapshot` is the sixth stable section and is deliberately **not** consumed: the recorded repomix `outputId` is session-scoped and dead in a forked session, so the pack is re-attached instead.

### The validation contract

Four rejections and one acceptance, all resolvable from `git` with no network fetch:

| Verdict               | Test                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **missing**           | `<root>/.claude/context/brief.md` does not exist                                       |
| **malformed**         | no `Base:` line, or any of the nine fixed `##` sections absent                         |
| **revision-mismatch** | `Base:` does not resolve, or is not an ancestor-or-equal of `HEAD`                     |
| **stale**             | `Base:` resolves and is contained in `HEAD`, but is not the checkout's `origin/main`   |
| **valid**             | `Base:` equals `git rev-parse origin/main` **and** is an ancestor-or-equal of `HEAD`   |

The comparison target is `origin/main`, not `HEAD`, because that is what the brief actually records — [`explore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) writes `Base: <origin/main SHA>` and its own Phase 0 re-reads it against `origin/main`. Validating against `HEAD` would reject every brief written in a session whose branch had moved ahead — which chapter 14 describes as the normal explore session — putting the producer and the consumer in open disagreement about what "current" means. The ancestor test is the second half: it confirms the working tree actually contains the mapped revision, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` is what keeps "older revision of this history" (`stale`) distinguishable from "different history entirely" (`revision-mismatch`), as the acceptance criteria require.

Deliberately no `git fetch`: the checkout's `origin/main` ref is the base the orchestrator produced, and re-fetching would let an unrelated upstream merge fail a correctly primed run. Requiring `Base:` to equal `origin/main` also makes the later branch-from-up-to-date-`main` step a no-op in the happy path, so the tree the plan was drafted against is the tree it is implemented against.

**Preconditions the skill must state**, because both are silent failures otherwise:

- **The brief is untracked.** `.claude/context/` is in `.gitignore`, so git will never carry `brief.md` into the forked checkout. # Add a strict run path for pre-primed explore sessions

## Pre-Implementation

Work happens on a new `issue-490-<slug>` branch created from an up-to-date `main`, so the pull request can close issue #490 on merge. The current worktree sits on a stale-merged branch 26 commits behind the base, so `main` is re-synced before the branch is cut — otherwise the work would carry finished history and would not even see the `explore` and `gather-context` skills it depends on.

## Summary

Add `/autopilot:run-primed`, a separate strict entry point that consumes a SHA-validated `.claude/context/brief.md` in place of the broad codebase pass, and extend `gather-context` with a third `Scope` value so the primed path still resolves everything the brief cannot bake in advance. `/autopilot:run` is untouched.

Steelmanned intent: A separate, explicit `/autopilot:run-primed` entry point that consumes a SHA-validated explore brief instead of the broad context fan-out, and fails loudly rather than silently downgrading to `run`.

Score: 90/100 — weakest dimension **Testability**, explained under [Verification](#verification).

## Context

[Issue #490](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/490) describes an orchestration pattern that today buys nothing: run [`/autopilot:explore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) once on an immutable revision, persist the transcript and the durable brief, fork the session into a clean checkout of that same revision, then implement a tracked issue. Step four must call [`/autopilot:run`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md), whose Phase 1 unconditionally re-runs the entire [`gather-context`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md) fan-out. The forked transcript is visible to the model but is not an authoritative input, so the repository is mapped twice.

That contract is correct for interactive `run` and must stay. The fix is a second, explicit door — not a heuristic inside `run` that tries to decide whether conversation history can be trusted. A file on disk carrying a base SHA is checkable; a prompt claiming "context was already gathered" is not.

Two decisions were taken with the requester before drafting. The acceptance criterion asking for tests over valid / missing / stale / revision-mismatch briefs is satisfied by a **discovery-driven guard test over the skill markdown**, the way every other skill in this repository is tested ([`planFileOutputPurity.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/planFileOutputPurity.test.ts), [`sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts)) — no bundled validator runtime and no new workspace scaffolding.
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     /autopilot:run-primed                      │
└───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                │ ①
                                ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Phase 1 — Validate .claude/context/brief.md                   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  present?  ·  parses?  ·  Base: resolves?  ·  Base: is base?   │
└───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┘
                │ ②                              │ ③
                ▼                                ▼
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓   ┌───────────────────────────────┐
┃  Abort                     ┃   │  Phase 2                      │
┃  missing · malformed       ┃   │  gather-context Scope: primed │
┃  stale · revision-mismatch ┃   └───────────────┬───────────────┘
┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛                   │ ④
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 3 — Preflight verdict  │
                                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                                 ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                 │  Phase 4 — Draft · review     │
                                 │  · score · finalize           │
                                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                 │ ⑤
                                                 ▼

                                 └───────────────────────────────┘
```

## Pre-Implementation

Work happens on a new `issue-490-<slug>` branch created from an up-to-date `main`, so the pull request can close issue #490 on merge. The current worktree sits on a stale-merged branch 26 commits behind the base, so `main` is re-synced before the branch is cut — otherwise the work would carry finished history and would not even see the `explore` and `gather-context` skills it depends on.

## Summary

Add `/autopilot:run-primed`, a separate strict entry point that consumes a SHA-validated `.claude/context/brief.md` in place of the broad codebase pass, and extend `gather-context` with a third `Scope` value so the primed path still resolves everything the brief cannot bake in advance. `/autopilot:run` is untouched.

Steelmanned intent: A separate, explicit `/autopilot:run-primed` entry point that consumes a SHA-validated explore brief instead of the broad context fan-out, and fails loudly rather than silently downgrading to `run`.

Score: 90/100 — weakest dimension **Testability**, explained under [Verification](#verification).

## Context

[Issue #490](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/issues/490) describes an orchestration pattern that today buys nothing: run [`/autopilot:explore`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/explore/SKILL.md) once on an immutable revision, persist the transcript and the durable brief, fork the session into a clean checkout of that same revision, then implement a tracked issue. Step four must call [`/autopilot:run`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/run/SKILL.md), whose Phase 1 unconditionally re-runs the entire [`gather-context`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/claude-plugins/autopilot/skills/gather-context/SKILL.md) fan-out. The forked transcript is visible to the model but is not an authoritative input, so the repository is mapped twice.

That contract is correct for interactive `run` and must stay. The fix is a second, explicit door — not a heuristic inside `run` that tries to decide whether conversation history can be trusted. A file on disk carrying a base SHA is checkable; a prompt claiming "context was already gathered" is not.

Two decisions were taken with the requester before drafting. The acceptance criterion asking for tests over valid / missing / stale / revision-mismatch briefs is satisfied by a **discovery-driven guard test over the skill markdown**, the way every other skill in this repository is tested ([`planFileOutputPurity.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/planFileOutputPurity.test.ts), [`sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts`](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/blob/main/.github/actions/code-review-action/src/sharedRulesInvocation.test.ts)) — no bundled validator runtime and no new workspace scaffolding. ┃  stale · revision-mismatch ┃   └───────────────┬───────────────┘

Base directory for this skill: /Users/tony_vi/.claude/plugins/cache/code-assistants/autopilot/1.14.0/skills/branch:create

# Create Branch

Create a git branch following the repository's naming conventions with GitHub or Linear issue integration. Supports GitHub issue branches (`issue-<number>-<slug>`), Linear ticket branches (`<team>-<number>-<slug>`), and special prefix branches (hotfix, trivial, maintenance, proposal, security).

## When to Use

- When creating a new branch from a GitHub issue
- When creating hotfix, trivial, maintenance, proposal, or security branches
- When invoked from `/autopilot:plan` for automatic branch creation
- When invoked from other skills

## Input

Arguments: `490`

Expected forms:

- `<ISSUE-NUMBER>` — GitHub issue number (e.g., `123` or `#123`). Used to fetch the issue and to build the branch name `issue-<number>-<slug>`.
- `<LINEAR-ID>` — Linear identifier (e.g., `ENG-123`, matching `^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$`) when the project lists a `linear` tracker in `package.json` `agents.trackers`. Builds `<team>-<number>-<slug>` (the id lowercased).
- `<ISSUE-NUMBER|LINEAR-ID> "<description>"` — issue identifier plus custom branch slug description
- `--start` — Linear only: also move the Linear ticket to "In Progress" after the branch is created (best-effort). Ignored for GitHub and special-prefix branches.
- `--hotfix "<description>"` / `--trivial "<description>"` / `--maintenance "<description>"` / `--proposal "<description>"` / `--security "<description>"` — special prefix branches without a GitHub issue (use `--security` for code-scanning alert fixes → `security-<slug>`)
- `--autopilot` — non-interactive mode used by `/autopilot:run`. Skips the [Phase 5](#phase-5-confirm-special-prefix-branch-name) confirmation prompt, which only special-prefix branches still reach. Issue and Linear branches are created directly for every caller, so the flag has no effect on them. Conflict resolution ([Phase 4](#phase-4-check-for-conflicts)) and validation errors still surface.

## Input resolution

Arguments are optional. When `490` is empty OR a field is missing, resolve from context in this order:

- **Issue number** — `490` → parse current branch name for `^issue-([0-9]+)` → prompt user only if none found and no special prefix flag is present.
- **Description** — `490` → generate from GitHub issue title via [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug) rules → no user prompt (auto-generate always succeeds).
- **Special prefix flags** (`--hotfix` / `--trivial` / `--maintenance` / `--proposal` / `--security`) — `490` only. Never inferred. Default: none.
- **`--autopilot`** — `490` only. Never inferred. Default: `false` (interactive mode).
- **Repository conventions** — read `CONTRIBUTING.md` directly from the repository root.

## Phase 0: Preflight Check

Invoke `Skill(autopilot:preflight-check)` with `mode: branch` from this conversation context. The skill validates current branch state, detects stale merged branches, and ensures main is up to date before a new branch is created. If it outputs a "cancelled" message, stop immediately — do not proceed to [Phase 1](#phase-1-input-validation).

## Phase 1: Input Validation

1. **Parse `490`** (shell-quoted positional tokens):
   - Check for `--autopilot`: if present, strip it from the arguments and set `autopilotMode = true`. Otherwise `autopilotMode = false`.
   - Check for `--start`: if present, strip it and set `startIssue = true` (Linear only; see [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute)). Otherwise `startIssue = false`.
   - Check for special prefix flags: `--trivial`, `--hotfix`, `--maintenance`, `--proposal`, `--security`
   - If flag found: extract description from remaining arguments
   - If no flag: extract the first argument as the issue identifier (GitHub number or Linear id), optional description
   - If `490` is empty, fall back to Input resolution (see above).

2. **If special prefix flag detected:**
   - Try to extract description from the conversation history
   - Description is REQUIRED — error if missing: `Description is required for special prefix branches (e.g., /autopilot:branch-create --trivial "fix typo")`
   - Multiple prefix flags not allowed — error: `Only one special prefix flag allowed`
   - Skip [Phase 2](#phase-2-fetch-github-issue) (no GitHub issue to fetch)

3. **If no flag, validate the issue identifier and resolve the provider** (read `package.json` `agents.trackers` with the Read tool):
   - **Linear** — the identifier matches `^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$` (e.g., `ENG-123`) AND a `linear` tracker is configured: set `provider = linear`.
   - **GitHub** — the identifier matches `^#?[0-9]+$` (strip a leading `#`): set `provider = github`.
   - If invalid: `Invalid issue identifier. Expected a GitHub number (e.g., 123 or #123), a Linear id (e.g., ENG-123) for a linear-tracked project, or a --trivial/--hotfix/--maintenance/--proposal/--security flag`

## Phase 2: Fetch GitHub Issue

**Skip this phase entirely for special prefix flag branches (--hotfix, --trivial, --maintenance, --proposal, --security).**

**If `provider` is `linear`:** fetch the ticket via the Linear MCP `get_issue` tool with `{ "id": "<LINEAR-ID>" }` and read its `title` (for the slug) and `state.name`; if no Linear MCP tool resolves (see the access note below), stop with its `No Linear MCP available …` message instead of continuing without ticket data. Skip the GitHub `gh` steps below and do NOT self-assign — Linear assignment is deferred to a later phase; emit `unassigned — Linear assignment deferred`. Then continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug). The steps below apply to **GitHub** issues only.

**Linear MCP access:** Read [`linear-mcp-access.md`](../shared-rules/references/linear-mcp-access.md) and apply its tool-resolution rule, using the bare tool names `get_issue`, `list_issue_statuses`, `save_issue`.

1. **Determine the repository** and bind it to `REPO` so every `gh` call in this phase targets the same repo (important in worktrees and multi-remote checkouts):

   ```bash
   REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner)
   ```

2. **Fetch the issue** (include `assignees` so the self-assign step needs no extra call):

   ```bash
   gh issue view <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --json title,body,state,assignees
   ```

3. **Extract:**
   - Issue title (for slug generation)
   - Issue body (for context)
   - Current state (warn if already closed)

4. **If issue not found:**
   - Error: `Issue #<ISSUE-NUMBER> not found in <repo>`

5. **Self-assign the current user** — idempotent and best-effort; it must never block branch creation.

   <!-- Canonical: [resolve-issue-context.md Phase 2](../../agents/resolve-issue-context.md#phase-2-auto-assign-current-user-opt-in) — keep this self-assign algorithm (statuses + steps) in sync with it. -->

   Assigning the issue the moment work starts keeps "who is working on what" accurate. This runs on every issue branch (special-prefix branches skip [Phase 2](#phase-2-fetch-github-issue), so they never assign). On ANY failure, emit the status line and continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug) — the branch is the deliverable; assignment is a side effect.

   Emit exactly one status (same vocabulary as the canonical agent):
   - `@<login> (just assigned)`
   - `@<login> (already assigned)`
   - `unassigned — gh not authenticated`
   - `unassigned — issue closed`
   - `unassigned — permission denied or assignee limit reached`
   - `unassigned — gh edit error: <first line of stderr>`

   Resolve it with these steps:
   1. Resolve the authenticated login (cached 5 minutes):

      ```bash
      LOGIN=$(gh api user --cache 5m --jq .login 2>/dev/null)
      ```

      If `LOGIN` is empty → `unassigned — gh not authenticated`; continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

   2. If the issue `state` from step 2 is `CLOSED` → `unassigned — issue closed`; continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

   3. Check whether `LOGIN` is already assigned. GitHub logins are `[A-Za-z0-9-]`, so the login is safe to interpolate into a single `gh --jq` expression (gh's `--jq` cannot take `--arg`); `.assignees[]?` tolerates a null or absent array:

      ```bash
      ALREADY=$(gh issue view <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --json assignees --jq "any(.assignees[]?; .login==\"$LOGIN\")" 2>/dev/null)
      ```

      If `ALREADY == "true"` → `@<LOGIN> (already assigned)`; continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

   4. Otherwise attempt the assignment, capturing stderr and exit code (keep this order; read `$?` on the very next line):

      ```bash
      STDERR=$(gh issue edit <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --add-assignee "$LOGIN" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
      EDIT_EXIT=$?
      ```

   5. **Only when `EDIT_EXIT == 0`**, post-verify with a fresh read, because `gh issue edit --add-assignee` returns exit 0 even when GitHub silently drops the addition (caller lacks `triage`/`write` permission, or the issue is at the 10-assignee limit). When `EDIT_EXIT != 0` the edit never landed, so skip this read and emit `unassigned — gh edit error: <first line of $STDERR>` directly:

      ```bash
      VERIFIED=$(gh issue view <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --json assignees --jq "any(.assignees[]?; .login==\"$LOGIN\")" 2>/dev/null)
      ```

      - `EDIT_EXIT == 0` AND `VERIFIED == "true"` → `@<LOGIN> (just assigned)`
      - `EDIT_EXIT == 0` AND `VERIFIED != "true"` → `unassigned — permission denied or assignee limit reached`
      - `EDIT_EXIT != 0` → `unassigned — gh edit error: <first line of $STDERR>`

   In all cases, continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

## Phase 3: Generate Branch Slug

**If special prefix branch:**

1. Normalize description to lowercase kebab-case
2. Remove special characters (keep only `a-z0-9-`)
3. Construct branch name: `<prefix>-<slug>` (prefix lowercased)
4. Example: `--hotfix` + `"memory leak in editor"` → `hotfix-memory-leak-editor`; `--security` + `"tainted format string"` → `security-tainted-format-string`
5. Validate total length ≤ 100 characters — if over 60, suggest shorter description; if over 100, require it

**If custom description provided:**

1. Normalize to lowercase kebab-case
2. Remove special characters (keep only `a-z0-9-`)
3. Use as the slug

**If no description provided:**

1. Analyze issue title and body
2. Generate a short, meaningful business-focused slug
3. **Rules:**
   - Paraphrased/summarized, NOT mechanical title-to-slug conversion
   - Lowercase with hyphens only
   - 3-5 words maximum
   - Capture the essence of what's being done

**Examples:**

| Issue Title                                                           | Generated Slug       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| "Add JWT token refresh endpoint for authentication service"           | `jwt-refresh`        |
| "Fix race condition in audio streaming when multiple clients connect" | `audio-race-fix`     |
| "Implement user preference settings page with dark mode toggle"       | `user-preferences`   |
| "Refactor database connection pooling for better performance"         | `db-pool-refactor`   |
| "Provide agent prompt to generate branch name"                        | `branch-name-prompt` |

**Construct full branch name:**

- **GitHub:** `issue-<number>-<slug>`
- **Linear:** `<team>-<number>-<slug>` — the Linear id lowercased, then the slug (e.g. `ENG-123` → `eng-123-<slug>`)
- Aim for under 60 characters; reject if over 100
- If too long: regenerate shorter slug

## Phase 4: Check for Conflicts

**Formatting Note:** Read [`askuserquestion-format.md`](../shared-rules/references/askuserquestion-format.md) and apply it before composing the `question` parameter.

1. **Check local branches:**

   ```bash
   git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch-name>
   ```

2. **Check remote branches:**

   ```bash
   git ls-remote --heads origin <branch-name>
   ```

3. **Handle conflicts using AskUserQuestion tool:**

   If branch exists locally or remotely, present options:

   Tool parameters:
   - `question`: "Branch <branch-name> already exists. How would you like to proceed?"
   - `header`: "Conflict"
   - `options`: [
     { label: "Checkout existing", description: "Switch to the existing branch" },
     { label: "Create with suffix", description: "Create <branch-name>-2" },
     { label: "Different description", description: "Enter a new description for the slug" }
     ]
   - `multiSelect`: false

## Phase 5: Confirm Special-Prefix Branch Name

**Issue-input bypass:** If `provider` is `github` or `linear`, skip this entire phase and proceed directly to [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute) with the resolved branch name. Do NOT call AskUserQuestion. The name is derived from an issue the user already chose, so confirming it carries no decision — and a name that turns out wrong costs a rename before any PR exists.

**Autopilot bypass:** If `autopilotMode` is true (from [Phase 1](#phase-1-input-validation)), skip this entire phase and proceed directly to [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute) with the resolved branch name. Do NOT call AskUserQuestion.

Only special-prefix branches (`--hotfix`, `--trivial`, `--maintenance`, `--proposal`, `--security`) reach this phase: their prefix and slug come from a free-form description rather than from an issue, so there is a real choice to confirm. Present branch details and confirm using **AskUserQuestion tool**.

**Preview substitution rules (MANDATORY):** The `<prefix>`, `<PREFIX>`, and `<slug>` tokens in the template below are PLACEHOLDERS. Before invoking AskUserQuestion, substitute each with the concrete value you resolved in earlier phases (e.g., `<prefix>` → `hotfix`, `<PREFIX>` → `HOTFIX`, `<slug>` → `memory-leak-editor`). NEVER pass the literal `<prefix>-<slug>\n\nType: <PREFIX>...` string — every option's `preview` must contain the fully resolved branch preview string. No shorthand (`"..."`, `"<same>"`, empty string) is permitted; always write out the full resolved preview for every option.

**One dialog template.** Tool parameters:

- `question`: "Review the branch name and choose an action."
- `header`: "Create branch"
- `options`: [
  { label: "Create branch", description: "Create and push to origin with tracking", preview: "<preview>" },
  { label: "Edit slug", description: "Modify the branch name slug", preview: "<preview>" }
  ]
- `multiSelect`: false

Both options carry the same `<preview>` content since the user is choosing an action, not content; the shared preview enables a side-by-side layout in the UI. Substitute `<preview>` with `<prefix>-<slug>\n\nType: <PREFIX>\nFrom: origin/main` — e.g. `hotfix-memory-leak-editor\n\nType: HOTFIX\nFrom: origin/main`.

Only proceed to [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute) after user selects "Create branch". If "Edit slug" selected, ask for new slug and regenerate branch name.

## Phase 6: Execute

1. **Fetch latest remote and create branch from origin/main:**

   ```bash
   git fetch origin
   git checkout -b <branch-name> origin/main
   ```

2. **Push with tracking:**

   ```bash
   git push -u origin <branch-name>
   ```

3. **If `provider` is `linear` AND `--start` was passed:** move the ticket to "In Progress" — best-effort, never blocks the branch. Resolve the target state id with the Linear MCP `list_issue_statuses` tool for the ticket's team, then call the Linear MCP `save_issue` tool with `{ "id": "<LINEAR-ID>", "state": "<In Progress state>" }` — tool resolution per the [Phase 2](#phase-2-fetch-github-issue) Linear MCP access note. On success, emit `✓ Ticket <LINEAR-ID> moved to In Progress`; when no Linear MCP tool resolves under any prefix, emit `issue not started — no Linear MCP available (check /mcp or connect one)`; on any other failure, emit `issue not started — <reason>`. Always continue — but the emitted line MUST reach the step 4 output block, never only intermediate text.

4. **Output result:**

   ```
   ✓ Branch created: <branch-name>
   ✓ Pushed to origin with tracking

   Next steps:
   - Make your changes
   - Use /autopilot:commits-create to create commits
   - Use /autopilot:pr-create when ready
   ```

   When `--start` was passed for a Linear ticket, add the step 3 outcome line after the push confirmation — `✓ Ticket <LINEAR-ID> moved to In Progress` on success, or the `issue not started — <reason>` line on failure — so a skipped transition is visible in the final output, not just mid-run.

## Examples

An issue branch is created without a dialog; a special-prefix branch confirms via the one [Phase 5](#phase-5-confirm-special-prefix-branch-name) template. Two worked cases below; Linear follows the issue case and the other special prefixes follow the hotfix case.

### GitHub issue (auto-generated slug)

```
/autopilot:branch-create 123

Fetching GitHub issue #123...
Title: "Add JWT token refresh endpoint for authentication service"
```

No confirmation dialog — the name is derived from the issue, so [Phase 5](#phase-5-confirm-special-prefix-branch-name) is skipped and the branch is created directly.

```
✓ Branch created: issue-123-jwt-refresh
✓ Pushed to origin with tracking
```

### Special prefix (--hotfix)

```
/autopilot:branch-create --hotfix "memory leak in editor"
```

AskUserQuestion with the [Phase 5](#phase-5-confirm-special-prefix-branch-name) template, both options' `<preview>` resolved to `hotfix-memory-leak-editor\n\nType: HOTFIX\nFrom: origin/main`.

User selects "Create branch".

```
✓ Branch created: hotfix-memory-leak-editor
✓ Pushed to origin with tracking
```

### Branch already exists

```
/autopilot:branch-create 123

Branch issue-123-jwt-refresh already exists locally.
```

AskUserQuestion with:

- `question`: "Branch issue-123-jwt-refresh already exists. How would you like to proceed?"
- `header`: "Conflict"
- `options`: Checkout existing / Create with suffix / Different description

User selects "Checkout existing".

```
✓ Switched to branch: issue-123-jwt-refresh
```

## Reference formatting

Before writing any output that mentions a file, standard, section, commit, or issue, read [`reference-formatting.md`](../shared-rules/references/reference-formatting.md) (RFC-0001) and apply it verbatim — link files, docs, skills, agents, and sections, and never leave a reference as bare text.

**Reference self-check (MANDATORY):** after composing the output, re-read it against [`reference-formatting.md`](../shared-rules/references/reference-formatting.md). A bare commit SHA, a bare tracker id outside a magic-word line, or an unlinked mention of a file that exists in the repo is a violation — fix it before emitting.

Branch-create Phase 0 (preflight) is already satisfied — the plan's preflight verdict ran during planning and concluded "stale-merged, re-sync and branch fresh", which is exactly what Phase 6 does by branching from a freshly fetched `origin/main`. Running the interactive check again would re-ask a settled question.
